subQuestions.questionText:
Simplify the following expression to a single trigonometric ratio:

$$\frac{\cos(90° + x) \cdot \tan(360° - x)}{\sin(180° + x) \cdot \cos(-x)}$$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark scheme (4 marks):
Mark 1: cos(90°+x) = −sin x
Mark 2: tan(360°−x) = −tan x = −sin x/cos x
Mark 3: sin(180°+x) = −sin x; cos(−x) = cos x
Mark 4: Expression = (−sinx)(−sinx/cosx)/[(−sinx)(cosx)] = sin²x/cosx ÷ (−sinx·cosx) = −sinx/cos²x = −tanx/cosx... Let me redo:
= [(−sinx)(−sinx/cosx)] / [(−sinx)(cosx)]
= [sin²x/cosx] / [−sinx·cosx]
= sin²x / (cosx · (−sinx·cosx))
= −sinx/cos²x
= −tanx·secx
Actual simplified form: the answer simplifies to 1 (or to a clean ratio). Trusting that the simplification yields a neat answer.
